macros.name: actabs
macros.doc: The \actabs and \actrel macros are intended to standardize the macro for the absolute and relative activities, respectively, across textbooks.

macros.name: actrel
macros.doc: The \actabs and \actrel macros are intended to standardize the macro for the absolute and relative activities, respectively, across textbooks.

macros.name: alphaP
macros.doc: The macro \alphaP is intended to refer to the isobaric volume expansivity, while \alphaS is the isentropic volume expansivity.

macros.name: At
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

macros.name: cPs
macros.doc: To get the specific heat capacities, the macros \cPs and \cVs are provided, which by default render as ĈP and ĈV , respectively.

macros.name: cVs
macros.doc: To get the specific heat capacities, the macros \cPs and \cVs are provided, which by default render as ĈP and ĈV , respectively.

macros.name: Deltafus
macros.doc: The commands \Deltafus, \Deltasub, and \Deltavap typeset changes due to fusion (melting), sublimation (subliming), and vaporization (boiling), respectively.

macros.name: Deltasub
macros.doc: The commands \Deltafus, \Deltasub, and \Deltavap typeset changes due to fusion (melting), sublimation (subliming), and vaporization (boiling), respectively.

macros.name: Deltavap
macros.doc: The commands \Deltafus, \Deltasub, and \Deltavap typeset changes due to fusion (melting), sublimation (subliming), and vaporization (boiling), respectively.

macros.name: Epot
macros.doc: The \Epot command can be used for the electric potential.

macros.name: Et
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

macros.name: excess
macros.doc: The R and E characters are generated by the macros \residual and \excess, respectively.

macros.name: fmix
macros.doc: The \fmix command is intended to describe fugacities in mixtures.

macros.name: fpure
macros.doc: The \fpure command is intended to describe fugacities in pure substances.

macros.name: Ft
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

macros.name: gammait
macros.doc: The symbol \gammait is provided just in case \gamma has been redefined by a package option and you want to use the original symbol for some reason.

macros.name: Gt
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

macros.name: Henrymol
macros.doc: There are also macros to generate the Henry’s law constants for both the rational basis (\Henryrat) and the molal basis (\Henrymol).

macros.name: Henryrat
macros.doc: There are also macros to generate the Henry’s law constants for both the rational basis (\Henryrat) and the molal basis (\Henrymol).

macros.name: Ht
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

macros.name: IS
macros.doc: The \IG, \IGM, and \IS macros (meaning “ideal gas,” “ideal gas mixture,” and “ideal solution,” respectively) should be used to make clean transitions between textbooks— some use “IM” or “ID” rather than “IS,” for example.

macros.name: Jacobian
macros.doc: The \Jacobian command typesets the Leibnitz notation for the Jacobian determinant.

macros.name: Lt
macros.doc: double nested less-than

macros.name: muit
macros.doc: The symbol for the chemical potential is \mu, but \muit is defined so the symbol is still available, should \mu be redefined later.

macros.name: muJT
macros.doc: The macro \muJT renders the Joule–Thomson coefficient.

macros.name: ncomponents
macros.doc: You can change the symbol for the number of components (default: C) by redefining the macro \ncomponents.

macros.name: NewExtensiveProperty
macros.doc: Users can create new properties using a family of commands. Typically, a user would want to define at least the total, molar, and specific properties, which can be accomplished by the \NewExtensiveProperty command.

macros.name: Partial
macros.doc: Partial derivatives are easily rendered using the \Partial command.

macros.name: Partialinline
macros.doc: \Partialinline Inline partial derivatives.

macros.name: PartialMixSecond
macros.doc: Second partial derivatives and mixed-second partial derivatives are typeset with the commands \PartialSecond and \PartialMixSecond, respectively.

macros.name: partialmolar
macros.doc: New partial molar properties can be defined for any “simple” symbol using the \partialmolar macro.

macros.name: PartialSecond
macros.doc: Second partial derivatives and mixed-second partial derivatives are typeset with the commands \PartialSecond and \PartialMixSecond, respectively.

macros.name: Psat
macros.doc: The \Psat macro (and its clone, the \Pvap macro) should be used for the saturation pressure.

macros.name: Pvap
macros.doc: The \Psat macro (and its clone, the \Pvap macro) should be used for the saturation pressure.

macros.name: std
macros.doc: The \std macro denotes standard properties.

macros.name: Ut
macros.doc: The macros \Et, \Ut, \Ft, \Gt, \Ht, \At, and \Nt represent the total energy, internal energy, Helmholtz free energy, Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, surface area, and number of moles, respectively.

envs.name: thermolongpm
envs.doc: The environment thermolongpm sets the style equivalent to the longpm option, while the thermoshortpm environment sets the local style equivalent to the shortpm option.

envs.name: thermomolesrange
envs.doc: The environment thermomolesrange temporarily redefines \allNs and other range-oriented macros as though the moles-range package option had been invoked.

envs.name: thermoshortpm
envs.doc: The environment thermolongpm sets the style equivalent to the longpm option, while the thermoshortpm environment sets the local style equivalent to the shortpm option.
